newsitem.title: ITALY: Mafia boss hangs himself in Italian jail.
newsitem.headline: Mafia boss hangs himself in Italian jail.

text.p: A lieutenant of Mafia godfather Salvatore "Toto" Riina, hanged himself in a Milan jail on Sunday, prison officials said.

They said Giacomo Giuseppe Gambino, 55, was still alive but wheezing when a warder at the San Vittore jail found him hanging in his cell. Despite efforts to revive him, Gambino died shortly afterwards.

Officials said he appeared to have tied a sheet around his neck. Gambino, who had been in jail since 1994, had spent several days in the hospital wing and feared he was suffering from a tumour, they said.

Gambino, known as "u tignusu" or "the bald one", had sat on the Sicilian Mafia's ruling "cupola" and was one of Riina's right-hand men who had betrayed their own bosses, relatives and friends to further the supremacy of Riina's Corleonesi clan.
He was one of the bosses sentenced in a major Mafia trial in the Sicilian capital Palermo in 1987 and had a record of multiple murder, possession of explosives and drug dealing.
Gambino was charged with involvement in many of the Mob's most spectacular killings, including the murder of star anti-Mafia judge Giovanni Falcone in 1992.
A string of top Mafia turncoats have highlighted his high-ranking place in the hierarchy of "Cosa Nostra", where he was believed to have been a key strategist of major attacks.

Two weeks ago, magistrates in Caltanisetta in central Sicily had charged him with involvement in the murder of Paolo Borsellino, another top anti-Mafia judge and close collaborator of Falcone, on the evidence of of turncoats.
Gambino was one of a few inmates in San Vittore held in strict isolation under a regime reserved for the most serious killers.
His lawyer, Franco Marasa, secured his transfer to Milan on health grounds and said Gambino suffered depression and heart problems.
Palermo magistrates had charged him with falsifying one of his heart tests with the collusion of a doctor and the case was due to have been examined in court on Friday.
